title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 88-90). X_n is the Riemann sphere carrying the 'dihedral' cell structure. Its features are:
- an n-gon on the equator, with vertices R_i and edge-midpoints Q_{a_i};
- the two poles P_ω (written P_0 and P_∞ elsewhere);
- the barycentric subdivision of this structure.
The rotation group D_n acts on it. The quotient map is g_n : X_n → X_0 = P^1_C.
- Vertices R go to 0, with infinite order, because they are removed: X_n^* = X_n minus the R_i.
- Edge-midpoints Q go to 1, with order 2.
- Poles go to ∞, with order n.
The real equator of P^1 is cut into the arcs (∞,0), (0,1), (1,∞).

Goal. Make explicit the isomorphism (97)/(98) between two groups:
- the D_n-equivariant fundamental group π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P), an extension of D_n by π_1(X_n^*);
- the orbifold fundamental group π_1(P^1, ∞·0 + 2·1 + n·∞; P_+) ≅ Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/n. This is the (∞,2,n) triangle group, with ρ_0 ρ_1 ρ_∞ = 1.
An element (ℓ, g) is sent to the class of g_n(ℓ). The base points are matched by a chosen path α: P_+ → P.

The computation on this page.
- The generator ρ (rotation of order n about the polar axis) is represented by the path α ρ(α)^{-1}. Deform it into X_n^{**} (X_n minus all ramification points) to a path α_ρ. This path crosses the 1-skeleton of the barycentric subdivision exactly twice: first an edge P_ω R mapping to the arc (∞,0), then the edge P_ω Q_{a_0} mapping to the arc (∞,1). The image is a loop at P_+ crossing (∞,0) then (∞,1), so g_n(ρ) = ρ_∞^{-1}.
- The half-turn σ_{a_0} = (λ_{a_0}, σ^0_{a_0}) about the axis through Q_{a_0} is represented by α_σ. This path crosses P_ω Q_{a_0} (image (∞,1)) and then Q_{a_0} R_0 (image (0,1)), giving ρ_1^{-1}.
- Another choice α'_σ crosses Q_{a_0} R_1 and then Q_{a_0} P_ω, giving ρ_1. Since ρ_1^2 = 1 in the quotient, ρ_1 = ρ_1^{-1} 'comme il se doit', so g_n(σ_{a_0}) = ρ_1.

Next page. It follows that g_n(ε_0) = g_n(σ_{a_0}ρ) = ρ_0. The isomorphism is then extended to D_n × {1, τ}, adding complex conjugation, i.e. reflection in a great circle.

What it serves. Within the 'Teichmülleries' notes, this is an explicit dictionary between the dihedral dessin (genus 0, Galois group D_n) and the triangle-group presentation. It is a building block for computing Galois / Teichmüller-tower actions on the dihedral (and polyhedral) dessins, including the real structure.
errors: No substantive error. g_n(σρ) = ρ_1^{-1} ρ_∞^{-1} = (ρ_∞ ρ_1)^{-1} = ρ_0 is consistent with the convention ρ_0 ρ_1 ρ_∞ = 1.
The signs of the images (ρ_∞^{-1} rather than ρ_∞) depend on orientation conventions for crossing equatorial arcs that are fixed on earlier pages; they cannot be independently checked from this page.
The final line was written by Grothendieck as a correction over the line; it should read g_n(σ_{a_0}) = ρ_1 (= ρ_1^{-1}).

ideas.what: Computing images of generators of an equivariant / orbifold fundamental group by counting the crossings of a lifted path with the edges of the barycentric subdivision (the dessin's triangulation). Each crossing is then translated into crossings of the real arcs of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial monodromy of dessins d'enfants; orbifold fundamental group of a Galois quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); developed by Jones–Singerman, Shabat–Voevodsky, Schneps and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dessins and regular polyhedra / dihedral maps in general terms; this explicit computation is not published as far as I know.

ideas.what: Isomorphism between the D_n-equivariant π_1 of the sphere minus the n vertices and the (∞,2,n) triangle group Z/2 * Z/n, with ρ ↦ ρ_∞^{-1}, σ_{a_0} ↦ ρ_1, ε_0 ↦ ρ_0.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group / Hecke-type triangle group of the dihedral dessin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (triangle groups); dessin viewpoint from Grothendieck and Jones–Singerman

ideas.what: Extension of the isomorphism to D_n × {1, τ}, including the anti-holomorphic reflection (complex conjugation) as part of the equivariant fundamental groupoid (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Extended (reflexible) triangle groups; real dessins; Gal(C/R) acting via fundamental groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck–Singerman and others for real / reflexible dessins

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine base-point and convention bookkeeping computation for the dihedral dessin. The result, that the D_n-equivariant π_1 is the (∞,2,n) triangle group with explicit generator images, is standard; nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ρ_1 et ρ_1^{-1} sont conjugués[?]' should read 'sont égaux', since ρ_1^2 = 1 in the quotient.
The quotient is written Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n⟩ (or Π_{03}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_0^n⟩ in Grothendieck's abbreviation), not ⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^2⟩.
The first edge crossed by α_ρ is written 'P_ω R_{a_1}' in the transcription; the image shows a vertex R (likely R_1).
The final displayed formula is g_n(σ_{a_0}) = ρ_1 (= ρ_1^{-1}), with the left side overwritten.
